turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_htsteel_process_train.csv: 300 real samples, columns
    process/composition columns (Fe, Cr, Ni, Mo, Mn, C, Ti, Si, Nb, V, P, B,
    Al, Cu, W, S, Heat treatment step 1 temperature, Heat treatment step 1 time, Heat treatment step 1
    cooling rate, Heat treatment step 2 temperature, Heat treatment step 2 time, Heat treatment step 2
    cooling rate, Heat treatment step 3 temperature, Heat treatment step 3 time, Heat treatment step 3
    cooling rate, Secondary treatment step 1 temperature, Secondary treatment step 1 time, Secondary treatment step 2
    temperature, Secondary treatment step 2 time, Secondary treatment step 3 temperature, Secondary treatment step 3
    time, Secondary treatment step 4 temperature, Secondary treatment step 4 time, Thermal exposure
    temperature, Thermal exposure time) and `target` (the measured yield strength
    at room temperature (MPa)).
  - b3_htsteel_process_pool.csv: 34 CANDIDATE samples whose yield strength
    at room temperature (MPa) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST yield
strength at room temperature (MPa), then select the 5 best candidates from
the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
# Analysis

The pool candidates all belong to a 13Cr martensitic/PH stainless steel family (Fe~84-86%, Cr~13%, Ni~0-0.6%, Mn~0.4-0.8%, C~0.2%), differing mainly in:
- **Heat treatment step 2 temperature** (ranging from 200°C to 740°C)
- **Aging (temper) treatment** (present vs. absent)
- Minor compositional variants (three near-identical base compositions, groups A/B/C)

**Key pattern from training data** (same alloy family, e.g. Fe≈84, Cr=13, Ni≈0.6, C≈0.12–0.4, Ti≈0.2, Cu≈0.3):

| HT2 temp | Aging | Target |
|---|---|---|
| 750°C | yes | 370 |
| 745°C | no | 580 |
| 650°C | yes | 670 |
| 600°C | yes | 820–840 |
| 540°C | no | 780 |
| 500°C | no | **1390** |
| 250°C | no | 930 |

This shows a **strong, consistent trend**: lower HT‑stage‑2 temperature (i.e., quenching from a lower intercritical/tempering temperature, retaining more untempered martensite) combined with **no subsequent aging/tempering step** produces dramatically higher yield strength. Composition (Ti/Cu microalloying, C content ~0.2) reinforces this effect.

Applying this to the pool:
- **Group C** (Ti=0.2, Cu=0.3, C=0.2, Mn=0.8) closely matches the highest-strength training analogs (930, 1390 MPa cases).
- **Group B** (C=0.205, no Ti/Cu) matches a slightly lower-strength analog (780 MPa at HT2=540).
- **Group A** (HT2 never below 715°C) has no low-temperature, no-aging candidates — predicted strengths stay modest (~400-600 MPa range).

Ranking pool candidates by (lowest HT2 temperature + absence of aging step + favorable composition group):

1. **c021** – Group C, HT2=200°C, no aging (best combination, composition matches highest training analogs)
2. **c017** – Group C, HT2=300°C, no aging
3. **c015** – Group B, HT2=200°C, no aging
4. **c018** – Group B, HT2=300°C, no aging
5. **c006** – Group C, HT2=450°C, no aging

Final: c021, c017, c015, c018, c006
